name: Elbow bend and straighten
summary: Standing or sitting, bend the elbow fully so the hand comes to the shoulder, then straighten it fully.
setup: Sit or stand side-on to the phone at chest height, working arm nearest, upper arm hanging by the side. Bend the elbow until the hand reaches the shoulder, then straighten fully. Keep the upper arm still.
brief: Sit or stand with the upper arm hanging by the side. Bend the elbow until the hand reaches the shoulder, then straighten fully.
why: From the side the shoulder–elbow–wrist angle runs from straight to fully bent each rep, and the upper arm swinging forward to help shows as the shoulder–elbow line leaving vertical.
dosage: 3 × 10, several times a day after injury.
progression: A light weight; a pause at each end.
regression: Support the upper arm on a table.
contraindications: Sharp pain or locking in the joint.

faults.label: Upper arm swinging forward
faults.tip: Pin the elbow to the side; only the forearm moves.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Not straightening fully
faults.tip: Full straightening is the range that gets lost after injury; finish each rep.

faults.label: Swinging from the shoulder
faults.tip: Pin the upper arm to your side so the movement is all at the elbow.

faults.label: Stopping short of the ends
faults.tip: Range is lost at the very ends. Go gently to both, every rep.
